message:
fix(directory): a trailing slash is not a different server

Whether a cached host token still belonged where it was issued was a string
comparison against the url as typed. So http://rem.example:8080/ and
http://rem.example:8080 were two servers, and so were http://rem.example and
http://rem.example:80 -- each mismatch threw the token away and registered
again. Nothing unsafe came of it; it just meant a trailing slash could cost
an unattended PC its credentials, which is the machine least able to type
them back in.

directory_origin_key() answers "same server?" and only that: the port is
always written out and the host lowercased, so defaults and case cannot make
one server look like two. The scheme stays in the key, because the fix must
not go the other way -- http and https are different origins and a token
issued to one has no business being sent to the other. Both comparison sites
use it, and what the user typed is still what is stored and shown, since
rewriting that under them is its own surprise.

The phone gets the same function and the same vectors.

Also here: the connect flow's observe decision moves out of the activity and
into DirectoryClient, with the health probe as a parameter. Three states
arrive there -- already known, learned from the health route, and not learned
at all -- and until now none of the branches could be reached from a test at
all, because reaching them meant standing up an Activity. Six of them are
now asserted, including the two that used to be one: a server that cannot be
reached and a server that answers but says nothing get different messages,
and on http a failed probe is not fatal because the documented default still
applies.

Checked while here and left alone: nothing in either client inserts a
hard-coded 29180 anywhere -- the port comes from the url or from what the
server advertised, and there is no third source.
